Gerber High-Efficiency Transformers, Inc. 3/21/10</p><p>CONCLUSIONS<br>A new optimized chip package is proposed to reduce the number of bit lines (BL) and contacts (C) over the conventional Darlington architecture with current maximum (CM) and minimum (MM) energy states. This new architecture also leads to better device matching and reduces skew between the chip and package geometry. For optimal device matching, the circuit efficiency is increased by employing the ground tree along with optimized wire routing. and establishes an optimal device matching. This improves pCB yield.</p></p><p>According to this approach, the complexity of a chip package is reduced by 15%.<br>2. INHERITANCE<br>The above chip packaging structure was achieved by adapting the most important key principles of an existing transformer design: (1) a ground/tree structure<br>(2) autopump/impedance matching and full compensation of the common mode voltage variation, and (3) short enable time by suppressing the equivalent series capacitance of the chip package.<br>On this ground/tree principle, we assume the first two implications: (1) wrap the core physically in a ring which respects patch arms of the ground/near ground tree and respects all chip symmetry (e.g., Kocon) and, (2) rely on the smaller width of the ring to suffice with be the longest bus line in the module with shortest bring time.</p></p> </p>
